PART B — LETTER TO THE GP

Date: 2026-11-07
Dear Colleague,
Re: patient identifiers not extracted — confirm from the patient record
Admitted 12/05 · Discharged 16/05 · Cardiology

Thank you for referring this 82-year-old female who was admitted with a 2-week history of central chest pain and shortness of breath on exertion, and was diagnosed with an NSTEMI.

ADMISSION SUMMARY:
ECG demonstrated T-wave inversion in V4-6 and troponin rose from 287 to 412. GRACE score was high risk. Creatinine was 168 on Day 2 (13/05), improving to 142 by Day 4 (15/05). Inpatient coronary angiogram confirmed severe three-vessel disease; following MDT review, the patient was deemed unsuitable for PCI and medical management was pursued. Dual antiplatelet therapy was commenced with ticagrelor alongside fondaparinux. Bisoprolol was uptitrated to 7.5mg once daily and isosorbide mononitrate 30mg once daily was added. She mobilised with physiotherapy and a cardiac rehabilitation referral was completed.

DIAGNOSIS:
Primary: NSTEMI

Secondary: Severe three-vessel coronary artery disease, not suitable for PCI — managed medically following MDT decision

Background:
- Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (EF 35%)
- Chronic kidney disease stage 3b
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus
- Hypertension
- Previous myocardial infarction 2019

RESUSCITATION STATUS
DNACPR. *** CHANGED DURING ADMISSION ***
Source: [L008]: "For resus."; [L012]: "For resus."; [L015–L016]: "DNACPR discussed + agreed w/ pt + family. DNACPR form completed by Dr Patel 14/05."

MEDICATIONS:
- Ramipril 5mg OD — CONTINUED [inferred from drug history — confirm]
- Bisoprolol 7.5mg OD — INCREASED (was 5mg OD)
- Furosemide 40mg OD — CONTINUED [inferred from drug history — confirm]
- Metformin 1g BD — CONTINUED [inferred from drug history — confirm]
- Atorvastatin 80mg ON — CONTINUED [inferred from drug history — confirm]
- Aspirin 75mg OD — CONTINUED [inferred from drug history — confirm]
- Ticagrelor — NEW
- ISMN 30mg OD — NEW

GP ACTIONS:
- Monitor renal function and uptitrate ACE inhibitor as tolerated

FOLLOW UP:
- Cardiology outpatient appointment in 6 weeks

SAFETY NET:
If you have been given a number to call, use that first. Otherwise, if you are worried, contact your GP or call NHS 111. Call 999 if it is an emergency.

Yours sincerely,
[Responsible clinician — name, grade, contact — to be completed]

Your discharge information

Why you were in hospital
You came in with chest pain and shortness of breath on exertion.

The team found you had:
- A heart attack (NSTEMI)
- Severe narrowing in three of the arteries supplying your heart

The team looked at your arteries and decided, after a team discussion, that an operation to open them up (PCI) was not suitable for you. They treated you with medicines instead.

What we did
While you were in hospital, the team:
- Did a heart tracing (ECG)
- Took blood tests to check your heart and kidneys
- Did a camera test of your heart arteries (coronary angiogram)

They treated you with:
- A blood-thinning injection (fondaparinux)
- A new antiplatelet medicine (ticagrelor), used alongside your existing antiplatelet medicine
- An increased dose of a heart medicine (bisoprolol), now 7.5mg once daily
- A new medicine for chest pain (isosorbide mononitrate) 30mg once daily
- Exercises with a physiotherapist to help you move around
- A referral to cardiac rehabilitation

Your medicines
- Ramipril 5mg once a day — keep taking as before [to be confirmed — in the drug history, not on the discharge list]
- Bisoprolol 7.5mg once a day — dose increased (was 5mg once a day)
- Furosemide 40mg once a day — keep taking as before [to be confirmed — in the drug history, not on the discharge list]
- Metformin 1g twice a day — keep taking as before [to be confirmed — in the drug history, not on the discharge list]
- Atorvastatin 80mg at night — keep taking as before [to be confirmed — in the drug history, not on the discharge list]
- Aspirin 75mg once a day — keep taking as before [to be confirmed — in the drug history, not on the discharge list]
- Ticagrelor — new medicine
- ISMN 30mg once a day — new medicine

What happens next
- You have a cardiology outpatient appointment in 6 weeks.
- Your GP will check your kidney function and may adjust your ACE inhibitor medicine as your body tolerates it.

Advice and getting help
If you have been given a number to call, use that first. Otherwise, if you are worried, contact your GP or call NHS 111. Call 999 if it is an emergency.
